sourceInformation.source: Pressure Cooker (1983), the arcade cooking video game
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGPU and WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio API; Gamepad API; AI Hub Session Protocol 1 client 1.4.0; WebRTC; BroadcastChannel; native JavaScript and CSS
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded 3D diner with ink outlines, cream, coral, mint and mustard colors, illustrated signs and contact shadows
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip chef breathing, walking and catch/serve actions; procedural conveyor, steam, particles and Rapier ingredient debris
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated swing jazz, kitchen sound effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices using Web Audio; music defaults to 10 percent; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–4-player shared-world co-op through AI Hub; standalone local-tab co-op using BroadcastChannel and remote direct WebRTC co-op using manual invite/answer codes
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium with software WebGPU and WebGL 2; complete scripted and AI playthroughs; emulated standard controller; touch and portrait profiles; OfflineAudioContext; local-tab and real WebRTC co-op; AI Hub 2-player, 4-player latency/jitter/loss, host-leave and dedicated-server scenarios. Physical controller, physical touch hardware and human listening: unknown
sourceInformation.research: No source research or internet searches. Native model knowledge; supplied AI Hub protocol read and dependency files downloaded for implementation

testingFeedback: Eleven tracked issues found through code review, scripted checks and visual validation: session activation, guest ticket selection, departed-player cleanup, round-end input/audio, controller menu controls, invite visibility, guest pause, controller disconnect, lobby start synchronization, hatch labels/colors and HUD readability. All were corrected.
Two blocked multiplayer features before correction: an inaccessible invite code and a guest pause lock. No startup or complete-playthrough failures remain.
The full fifteen-burger, three-shift scripted playthrough, paired with real two-page WebRTC and the AI Hub fault harness, gave the strongest coverage.
A headless WebGPU screenshot was blank. State assertions and a WebGL visual check were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL made quantized cel lighting straightforward, and AnimationMixer supplied a useful base for expressive procedural chefs.
Yes. WebGPU screenshots were blank in the headless environment, so I used state checks for WebGPU and the renderer's WebGL fallback for visual inspection.
The authoritative cooking simulation, recipe and shift tools, input navigation, and co-op lifecycle had to be built around the renderer.
Keeping WebGPU-compatible materials, native animation, physics poses and network snapshots readable and synchronized was the hardest integration work.
A small official reference combining WebGPU, physics, controller UI and reproducible headless capture would help.
promptFeedback: The specific source, coded-audio requirement and ten-foot controller philosophy gave the game a clear identity.
Standalone online did not specify hosted matchmaking or signaling. I implemented direct invite/answer codes alongside automatic AI Hub sessions.
Making the same complete kitchen loop work with keyboard, mouse, controller, touch and an authoritative online host was hardest.
Specify whether standalone online requires a hosted lobby service or whether direct connection codes are sufficient.

aiHub.name: Short Order Fever
aiHub.tagline: A little sizzle. A lot of heart.
aiHub.description: Catch fresh ingredients, stack exact burger orders and race them to matching hatches in a colorful ink-outlined diner. Serve fifteen burgers across three escalating shifts, solo or with up to four chefs.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD/arrows move; Cross/Space catch and serve; shoulders/Tab/1–3 select ticket; Square/Shift dash; Circle/Q toss; Triangle/E bell; Options/Esc pause; mouse click to move/interact; touch drag with assisted catches.
